title: Capacity & Price Elasticity Rotation Planner (Q1–Q4 FY27)
sheet_data:
Executive summary:
This working sheet maps a 4-quarter plan that links reserved GPU capacity, hiring phasing for serving and SRE, and a 3-scenario pricing sensitivity lattice. The goal is to produce a fast decision surface: for any observed demand delta (tokens / month) we can read recommended hiring pause/accelerate actions and price movement ranges to protect margin while preserving product SLAs.

Key assumptions (high-level):
- Baseline demand (Base): 1.8B tokens/month entering Q1 FY27, 20% QoQ natural growth without product changes.
- Latency SLA requires 95th percentile < 220ms for production routes; extra capacity required to maintain SLA under +30% burst.
- Reserved GPU mixes: 40% A100 80GB, 40% H100, 20% cheaper quantized instances (q8) for non-critical routes.
- Burden multiplier for total comp = 1.22 (salary + benefits + taxes + equipment).
- Price elasticity approximations derived from FY26 experiments: short-term elasticity = -0.65, medium-term = -1.1 when alternatives available.

Quarterly capacity & budget table (USD, simplified):
quarter, reserved_gpu_hours, spot_gpu_hours, avg_gpu_hour_cost, other_cloud_costs, total_compute_cost, other_opex
Q1-FY27, 55,000, 12,000, 4.20, 210,000, 450,000, 120,000
Q2-FY27, 62,000, 9,000, 4.00, 200,000, 488,000, 125,000
Q3-FY27, 74,000, 6,000, 3.85, 185,000, 548,900, 135,000
Q4-FY27, 88,000, 4,000, 3.60, 170,000, 620,800, 140,000

Notes on compute rows: total_compute_cost = reserved_gpu_hours * avg_gpu_hour_cost + spot_gpu_hours * (avg_gpu_hour_cost * 0.6) + other_cloud_costs. These numbers include expected compression/quantization routing savings (applied in Q3+).

Headcount phasing table (FTEs and comp):
role, base_fte_start_Q1, hire_plan_Q1, hire_plan_Q2, hire_plan_Q3, hire_plan_Q4, avg_salary, total_annualized_cost_estimate
Serving-engineer, 18, 2, 3, 4, 2, 170000, =FTEs*avg_salary*1.22
SRE, 8, 1, 1, 2, 1, 165000, =FTEs*avg_salary*1.22
Applied-ML, 10, 1, 2, 1, 1, 185000, =FTEs*avg_salary*1.22
Customer-success (technical), 6, 0, 1, 1, 0, 130000, =FTEs*avg_salary*1.22
Product, 7, 0, 1, 0, 1, 160000, =FTEs*avg_salary*1.22

Interpretation: hires are phased to Q2/Q3 to support 40–60% expected ramp in model rollout. Total incremental headcount incremental burn (comp+burden) projected "hit" in Q3 when most hires fully onboard; hiring ramp can be paused if revenue triggers breach thresholds in the sensitivity lattice below.

Pricing sensitivity lattice (scenario outputs given a +/−10/20/30% price move):
price_move_pct, short_term_elasticity, expected_rev_delta_pct, delta_rev_USD_Qtr, margin_impact_notes
-30, -0.65, +19.5, "Base rev 12M/4 per qtr -> +? (see note)", heavy revenue upside but risk of product cannibalization in enterprise discounts
-10, -0.65, +6.5, "+$480k (Q) estimated", modest uplift, limited churn observed in trials
0, -0.65, 0, $0, baseline
+10, -0.65, -6.5, "-$480k (Q)", reduces revenue; this compresses margin but reduces demand load
+20, -1.1, -22, "-$1.6M (Q)", large demand contraction likely to trigger hiring pause and reserve capacity release
+30, -1.1, -33, "-$2.4M (Q)", high risk: churn & SLA-impact planning required

Notes on the lattice: expected_rev_delta_pct = price_move_pct * elasticity (approx); short_term_elasticity used for immediate reaction; medium-term elasticity used for Q2+ planning. Delta revenue USD uses baseline run-rate assumption of $7.4M revenue per quarter (ARR/4 proxy used for quick math).

Trigger rules (operationalizable):
- If measured tokens/month growth (30-day lookback) < baseline - 15% AND revenue deviation > -8% vs plan -> pause non-critical hiring for next quarter, defer reserved GPU purchases if next 90-day utilization < 60%.
- If M/M tokens > +25% sustained for 3 weeks OR 95th p95 latency breach for two consecutive days -> accelerate hiring for serving by one cohort (2–3 hires) and commit to short-term spot pool increase (cap to 20% of additional capacity).
- If realized revenue delta (trailing 30 days) < -12% vs forecast -> consider +10% price increase experiment on non-enterprise routes for 21 days with A/B and rollback rule.

Operational playbook (step-by-step):
1) Weekly sync: finance + product + infra — publish utilization dashboard and run the trigger rules.
2) If trigger fires to pause hiring: HR notified, offer freeze window of 21 days; project managers to re-baseline deliverable dates.
3) If trigger fires to accelerate: Recruiting to prioritize server-side specializations; procurement to request short-term capacity add via reserved + market spot expansion.
4) Pricing experiment runbook: select 3 controlled routes, randomize 10% price bump for 10% of traffic, measure conversion and retention; automatic rollback if M7 churn > 1.2x baseline for cohort.

Sensitivity checks and edge cases:
- Elasticity uncertainty: run Monte Carlo where elasticity ~ Normal(mean=-0.85, sd=0.25) and compute revenue outcomes for price moves ±20%. If >= 20% of draws show revenue loss > $1.5M, do not implement price increase without product value comms.
- Latency interaction: lower-cost quantized routes may raise model hallucination rate; tagged as non-critical only. Budget includes remediation buffer of $150k / quarter to re-route traffic to high-fidelity instances if customer complaints exceed 0.8% of sessions.

Recommended next steps (for the finance + product committee):
- Approve hire-phasing but add a hard pause gate tied to the first trigger rule above.
- Authorize procurement to negotiate 3-month flexible reserves (convertible to spot within 60 days) up to 25% of Q3 planned reserved hours.
- Run 10% price bump experiment on non-enterprise routes for 21 days before end of Q1; finance to run Monte Carlo posterior and share results.

Appendix: quick calculation snippets and references:
- Example total comp calc: 3 new serving hires * $170k salary * 1.22 burden = $622,200 annualized incremental cost.
- Compute cost delta example: moving 10% of traffic to quantized path reduces avg_gpu_hour_cost by 0.35 USD but increases infra-engineering overhead by $18k/Q.
- Reference links: https://confluence.redwood/company/capacity-price-rotation, FIN-2453, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/cost-models/pull/87

Document notes: this sheet is intentionally a working artifact with quick formulas and trigger rules. Numbers are for planning/decisioning and should be validated in the canonical cost model repo above before executive sign-off.
